title: Reliability collab patterns & SLO soak plan — working notes
content:
Purpose and short summary:
This doc captures a lightweight, cross-functional pattern for running multi-week SLO soak experiments and operationalizing reliability improvements. The focus is on low-friction collaboration between product, serving-runtime, platform, and SRE so that we can validate SLOs under realistic load, identify ownership gaps, and bake safe rollout steps into runbooks.

Why a separate "soak" plan?
- Many reliability regressions appear only under sustained traffic patterns or unusual cache warmup characteristics. Short canary fails to reveal some classes of tail-latency or cache-pressure problems.
- A soak experiment gives teams a bounded way to exercise the full stack for 2–6 weeks with defined metrics and remedial hooks.

Scope and primary goals (measurable):
1) Validate 99th and 99.9th latency SLOs for the text-generation API under real request mixes for 21 days. Target: no more than 1.2x baseline error budget burn.
2) Surface cross-team ownership gaps (deploy rollback, KV-cache invalidation, autoscaler tuning). Track and resolve at least 80% of identified handoff issues during the soak window.
3) Produce runbook patches and a short list of config changes that reduce token cost without >5% latency regressions.

Stakeholders / contacts:
- SRE lead: Aisha Patel (owner)
- Serving runtime: Daniel Kim (kernel + batching)
- Platform/autoscaling: Priya Sharma
- Product/hosted-api: María González (product metrics lead)
- Observability: Liam O'Connor (traces + dashboards)
- Solutions Eng: Evan Brooks (customer-facing impact assessments)

Experiment cadence and phases (high level):
- Week -2: Prep & triage workshop. Confirm traffic replay datasets, gating metrics, and rollback criteria.
- Week -1: Dry-run in staging (48–72h) to validate dashboards and alerting.
- Week 0–3: Soak window (21 days) running a production-adjacent traffic mix in a controlled pool (dedicated namespace + tag).
- Week 4: Post-soak analysis and remediation sprints (2 weeks for quick fixes; larger items backlogged).

Control plane and safety gates (must-haves before starting):
- Canary cutoff: automated rollback if 5-min error rate >2x baseline AND 99.9 latency increases >30%.
- Manual guardrail: SRE on-call signoff required to extend beyond day 14.
- Resource cap: autoscaler configured to enforce a max-GPU cost guard at pool level.

Metrics to collect (minimum set):
- P95, P99, P99.9 latency for token generation and end-to-end request
- 1-min and 5-min error rate, broken down by error class (timeout, OOM, 4xx/5xx)
- KV-cache hit ratio and prefix cache warmup curve by model variant
- GPU utilization and queue-depth distribution
- Token cost per 1k tokens
- Observability coverage: traces per 1k requests, sample retention for tail traces

Ownership grid (quick mapping):
- Latency analysis: SRE + serving-runtime
- Autoscaler tuning: platform + SRE
- Cache invalidation bugs: serving-runtime + product (prompt formats)
- Customer-impact triage: solutions-eng + product

Friction map (expected failure modes and where they show up):
- Cache warmup vs. cold start: shows as early-day spike in P99, ownership split across runtime and request router. Action: add prefix pre-warm policy and track attr:prefix-warm.
- Autoscaler thrash: repeated scale-ups/downs under bursty but sustained load. Shows as queue growth and increased P99. Action: introduce hysteresis on scale-down and cap burst capacity for soak pool.
- OOMs triggered by long prompt tails: shows as 5xx with OOM. Ownership: runtime + product. Action: enforce conservative max sequence length and add circuit breaker.

Runbook changes we expect to produce (examples):
- SLO escalation ladder: add a mid-tier "Soak degraded" page with recommended mitigations (drain pool, pin earlier model variant, increase cache TTL).
- Tracing playbook: pre-baked trace queries for slow prefix detection and a saved trace-view in Observability.
- Rollback checklist: one-click rollback to stable model variant + autoscaler reset steps.

Communication plan (internal + customer-facing):
- Internal: weekly 30-min soak sync (SRE + runtime + platform + product). Daily 10-min standup during first 72 hours. Shared notes in the 'reliability-soak' channel.
- Customer-facing: triage updates via Solutions Eng for any customers hit by degraded latency > 99.9 SLO violation for >1 hour. Use standard incident template and attach planned mitigations.

Acceptance criteria for a successful soak:
- SLO burn for the window <= 1.2x projected budget AND no customer-facing incidents requiring manual rollback.
- All owner-assigned handoff tickets created and at least 80% have a mitigation or schedule for remediation.
- Runbook patches merged and validated in staging.

Quick checklist before kickoff:
- [ ] Traffic replay dataset verified and tagged (owner: María)
- [ ] Alert thresholds and dashboards validated (owner: Liam)
- [ ] Autoscaler safety caps configured (owner: Priya)
- [ ] On-call rotation scheduled for soak (owner: Aisha)
- [ ] Conformance test for trace sampling in place (owner: Liam)

Open questions / trade-offs (notes):
- How aggressively do we instrument token-level tracing during soak? More tracing helps diagnosis but increases cost and may affect latency profiles. Proposal: sampling ramp (1% baseline -> 5% during suspected anomalies).
- Should we allow model-quantization toggles during soak? Risk: changes performance characteristics mid-soak. Proposal: freeze quantization profile unless explicitly needed for remediation.

Immediate next steps (this week):
1) Triage workshop: confirm dataset and list of top-10 prior incidents to simulate. (Owner: Aisha)
2) Create soak dashboard and baseline runbook PR. (Owner: Liam)
3) Prep a lightweight cost-model showing max expected GPU spend for 21-day window and acceptable overage. (Owner: Priya)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the soak pool logically separate from customer production traffic; still aim for realistic mix (100% of token type distribution but only 10–30% absolute volume).
- If we see repeated prefix-related tail-latency, consider quick A/B of prefix-cache TTLs across two soak subpools.

References and related pages:
- Reliability experiments index: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/SRE/Reliability+Soak+Experiments
- Incident replay list: SRE-4321
- Observability saved views: saved_view:soak-p99-traces

-- end of working notes --
